item.text: [{"taxonId":51306,"summary":"An annual flowering crop reported as native from the eastern Mediterranean to India, common flax is known only as a cultivated plant. Its slender stems yield smooth, strong fibres used for linen, while its seeds are eaten or processed into edible flaxseed oil.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Seeds are eaten or ground into meal; flaxseed oil is edible, though solvent-processed oil has also long been used for painting and varnishing.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p4","s1:p7","s1:p13","s1:p34","s1:p35","s1:p37"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p34","s1:p37","s3:p2"]}},{"taxonId":51428,"summary":"A genus of green algae with a probably worldwide distribution, Chaetomorpha occurs in marine or brackish water and only very rarely in fresh water. Its visible filaments are unbranched and only one cell thick, with thick-walled cylindrical or barrel-shaped cells.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p2","s1:p5"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":51430,"summary":"An order of green algae found mainly in marine habitats, Cladophorales has also made four transitions into fresh water, while only two genera are terrestrial. Its attached filaments are one cell thick, contain many nuclei and range from unbranched to profusely branched.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p3"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":51618,"summary":"A herbaceous perennial native to the mountains of southern and central Europe, from the Pyrenees to the Caucasus. Its feathery leaves and softly hairy growth smell strongly of aniseed when crushed. Leaves are sometimes eaten raw or cooked; roots are cooked like parsnips, and seeds are chewed raw.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Leaves are eaten raw or cooked, roots are cooked like parsnips, and seeds are chewed raw.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p4","s1:p5","s1:p7"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p7"]}},{"taxonId":51637,"summary":"A grass genus native to tropical and warm-temperate regions, Digitaria comprises slender annual and perennial plants with long, finger-like flower clusters. Seeds of named members—including two fonio species, Digitaria sanguinalis and Digitaria compacta—are eaten in several forms.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Edible seeds include fonio species, D. sanguinalis and D. compacta; they may be toasted, made into flour or porridge, or fermented into beer.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p3"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p3"]}},{"taxonId":51734,"summary":"A perennial nightshade plant originating in Mexico, Physalis philadelphica bears small spherical green or green-purple fruit and is generally farmed as an annual. Its yellow flowers have blue anthers, and each berry fills or bursts a ten-ribbed husk. The fruit is a Mexican staple eaten raw or cooked, notably in salsa verde.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"The fruit is eaten raw or cooked in Mexican dishes, notably salsa verde.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p27"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p2"]}},{"taxonId":51737,"summary":"A mostly annual vine originating in western South America, the tomato bears an edible berry eaten as a vegetable.
